deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page builds the p-variable theta series with exponent sum a_{mu,mu'} m_mu m_mu'. That needs a_{mu,mu'} = a_{mu',mu} and a negative-definite real part. This page proves the symmetry. It is a draft of §20 of Riemann's 1857 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen'.

(1) Canonical dissection (top lines, partly cancelled). The (2p+1)-fold connected surface T is cut by cross-cuts a_1,...,a_p and b_1,...,b_p into a simply connected surface T'. Each b_nu is drawn from the negative side of a_nu, and a_{nu+1} is joined to the previous cuts by a connecting line. After this dissection each cross-cut appears twice in the boundary of T', once in each direction.

(2) Setup. Let w_1,...,w_p be linearly independent everywhere-finite integrals of rational functions of s and z (abelian integrals of the first kind, i.e. integrals of holomorphic differentials). Write A^nu_mu for the periodicity modulus of w_mu at the cross-cut a_nu, i.e. the jump w_mu^+ - w_mu^-, which is constant along a_nu. Write B^nu_mu for the modulus at b_nu.

(3) Vanishing boundary integral. Take the integral of w_mu dw_mu' positively around the boundary of T'. It is 0, because w_mu is single-valued on T' and the integrand is everywhere finite (Cauchy's theorem).

(4) Pairing of the two edges. Each cut is traversed twice with opposite orientation. Along it dw_mu' takes the same value on both edges, since the jump of w_mu' is constant. The two traversals therefore combine to the integral of (w_mu^+ - w_mu^-) dw_mu' along the cut.

(5) Evaluation on each cut. The b-lines lead from the positive to the negative side of the a-lines, and the a-lines from the negative to the positive side of the b-lines. Hence integrating dw_mu' along a_nu gives B^nu_mu', and along b_nu gives -A^nu_mu'. So:
- the contribution of a_nu is A^nu_mu * B^nu_mu';
- the contribution of b_nu is B^nu_mu * (-A^nu_mu').

(6) Result. Summing the contributions and using step (3):

sum_{nu=1}^p (A^nu_mu B^nu_mu' - B^nu_mu A^nu_mu') = 0 for all mu, mu'.

In matrix form, with A_{nu,mu} = A^nu_mu, this reads A^T B - B^T A = 0. The left side is antisymmetric in (mu, mu'), so this gives p(p-1)/2 independent relations among the periods, as the page says.

(7) Normalization. Choose the basis so that A^nu_mu = 0 for nu != mu and A^nu_nu = pi i. The relations become pi i (B^{mu'}_mu - B^mu_{mu'}) = 0. With a_{mu,mu'} := B^{mu'}_mu this is a_{mu,mu'} = a_{mu',mu}, the symmetry needed for the theta series on the previous page.

(8) Not on this page. The positivity part of the argument (Re a negative definite, via the area integral of |dw|^2) is not here. It is presumably treated elsewhere.
errors: Sign conventions: the final line is written as B^{mu'}_mu pi i - B^mu_{mu'} pi i = 0, which is the negative of what step (6) gives after normalization (pi i (B^mu_{mu'} - B^{mu'}_mu)). This is immaterial since the right side is 0.
Overall orientation signs depend on the side conventions in the partly cancelled opening lines. These cannot be fully read but do not affect the symmetry conclusion.
Implicit and unstated: dw_mu' is single-valued along each cut, so the two edges pair off. This is correct for differentials of the first kind.

results.what: For any two everywhere-finite abelian integrals w_mu, w_mu' with a/b-periods A, B: sum_nu (A^nu_mu B^nu_mu' - B^nu_mu A^nu_mu') = 0. This yields p(p-1)/2 relations, proved by integrating w_mu dw_mu' around the boundary of the dissected surface T'.
results.modern_name: Riemann bilinear relations (equality part) / symplectic period relations

results.what: With periods normalized to A^nu_mu = pi i delta_{nu,mu}, the b-period matrix a_{mu,mu'} is symmetric.
results.modern_name: Symmetry of the normalized period matrix (Riemann matrix, Siegel upper half-space condition)

results.what: Canonical dissection of a (2p+1)-fold connected surface by cross-cuts a_nu, b_nu into a simply connected T', each cut bordering T' twice in opposite directions.
results.modern_name: Canonical homology basis / canonical dissection (polygon model of a genus-p surface)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of exactly the argument published in Riemann's 1857 Abelian functions paper (§20), the famous bilinear relations proof. It is well known and attributed to him.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; b11,b12,b22=symbols('b11 b12 b22'); A=pi*I*eye(2); B=Matrix([[b11,b12],[b12,b22]]); simplify(A.T*B - B.T*A) == zeros(2)
checkable.asserts: With A = pi*i*I and B symmetric, the bilinear relation A^T B - B^T A = 0 holds.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; B=Matrix(2,2,symbols('c0:4')); A=pi*I*eye(2); solve(list(A.T*B - B.T*A), list(B.free_symbols))
checkable.asserts: Conversely, under the normalization A = pi*i*I the relations force B[0,1] == B[1,0], i.e. a_{mu,mu'} = a_{mu',mu}.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; p=symbols('p'); A=Matrix(3,3,symbols('a0:9')); B=Matrix(3,3,symbols('b0:9')); M=A.T*B-B.T*A; simplify(M+M.T)==zeros(3)
checkable.asserts: The matrix of relations is antisymmetric, so only p(p-1)/2 of the entries are independent (here p=3 gives 3).
